summary: The three original RAW_UNSCREENED proposals remain preserved. Literal packet checks expose a P01 page-coverage/boundary problem and realistic rivals for all three. None is empirically falsified; none presently supplies a meaning-bearing discriminator.

proposals.original_prediction: A shared qo kernel with a compositional eedy/teedy state-to-process contrast predicts qoteedy-to-qokeedy or qoteedy-to-qokedy pairings and stable successor classes in f77r.11, .14, .17, .20 and f85r1.2-.3.
proposals.scope_finding: qoteedy and qokeedy do not co-occur as exact forms on two physical pages; qoteedy is f77r-only. The f85r1.2-.3 observation broadens from qoteedy/qokeedy to otedy/qotedy/qokchdy, and the original t/k contrast is not an eedy/teedy contrast.
proposals.realistic_rival: A grammar or fixed whole-phrase template can place two frequent forms in the same line; qokeedy and qoteedy may be independent words with position-conditioned collocation.
proposals.why: Same-line co-occurrence on one page and related but nonidentical f85r1 forms cannot separate a compositional state/process meaning from a positional or whole-phrase grammar.
proposals.smallest_genuinely_different_consequence: An exact t/k opposition with the same controlled neighbors must recur on a second physical page and predict a different local content relation, or an in-packet matched context must show the t/k choice changing a relation while lexical/position controls remain fixed. The current packet supplies neither.
proposals.recommendation: Retain as raw exploratory wording only; do not select P01 or silently treat f85r1 related forms as exact qoteedy/qokeedy evidence.

proposals.original_prediction: ol shells preserve kernels and neighbor classes across f80v and f85r1, including olshedy-qokeedy at f77r.23 and f85r1.4, whereas unrelated wholes do not.

observations: f80v.30-.36 has a dense ol/olkain/olshey/olshedy/olky run
f77r.23 and f85r1.4 both contain olshedy qokeedy in ZL/IT

proposals.scope_finding: The observations are real packet forms, but shared morphology can itself produce kernel reuse and collocation. The original independent-whole rival is too weak because a whole-phrase or productive orthographic grammar can mimic both predicted signals without any stable meaning-bearing ol layer.
proposals.realistic_rival: A register-specific grammar licenses recurring ol-shaped whole phrases and collocations; apparent kernels are morphological coincidence or a formal construction with no portable content role.
proposals.why: Kernel overlap plus repeated olshedy qokeedy adjacency does not show that ol modifies content rather than belonging to a formal or phrase-level construction; GDT945/GDT946 already warn against generalizing ol/olal roles.
proposals.smallest_genuinely_different_consequence: Within matched contexts, one shell change must alter a declared relation while the kernel/content environment stays fixed, and the converse shell reuse must preserve that relation on a second paragraph; both outcomes must be scored against a morphology/whole-phrase null using raw boundaries.
proposals.recommendation: Retain as plausible untested composition, but do not select until a relation-changing consequence beyond kernel/collocation is written and available in scope.

proposals.original_prediction: RF marks and reader-specific spacing change surface segmentation while preserving an ordered kernel/relation-slot spine at f77r.23, f80v.32/.36 and f85r1.4.

observations: f77r.23 ZL/IT olshedy qokeedy chedy qok[a:o]l/qokol versus RF olshe@152;y qokeedy che@152;y qokal
f80v.32 ZL arolkeedy versus IT arol keedy is documented in GDT944, not as a ZL/IT separator flag in EXPOSED_PARAGRAPHS
f85r1.4 ZL/IT olshedy qokeedy versus RF olshe@152;y qokee@152;y

proposals.scope_finding: RF_VARIANTS preserves raw separator flags, but EXPOSED_PARAGRAPHS word arrays do not encode all ZL/IT flags. More fundamentally, ZL/IT/RF are alternate readings of one manuscript, so cross-reader agreement cannot be independent semantic evidence.
proposals.realistic_rival: Transcriber orthography, source copying, and whole-phrase alignment produce the same stable spine while carrying no semantic or compositional claim; RF marking can be a reader convention.
proposals.why: Invariant order across alternate transcriptions is expected from a shared source. Raw RF boundaries can audit transcription, but cannot by themselves identify a shared content role or meaning.
proposals.smallest_genuinely_different_consequence: A within-reader, raw-boundary-conditioned change in neighboring form/argument configuration must recur at a second locus against an explicit orthographic whole-phrase null; reader agreement alone is insufficient. No such independent semantic consequence is currently supplied.
proposals.recommendation: Retain only as an orthographic/segmentation hypothesis pending a non-reader discriminator; do not use it as independent semantic support.
